sections.normalized_html:
Two sets are equivalent if they contain the same elements. It doesn't matter if the elements are listed differently or if one set has duplicates and the other does not.

To determine which of the given sets is equivalent to [MATH: S,] we start by listing the elements of [MATH: S,] ignoring any duplicates: [MATH: 2, \qquad 4, \qquad 8]

Therefore, the only set equivalent to [MATH: S] is [MATH: \{2,4,8\}] since it contains the same elements as [MATH: S.]

The other sets are not equivalent to [MATH: S{:}]

  • [MATH: \{\{2\},4,8\}] has the element [MATH: \{2\}] that is not in [MATH: S.] Note that [MATH: \{2\}\neq 2].

  • [MATH: \{2,8\}] is missing the element [MATH: 4.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

On the other hand, if two sets [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] are not equivalent, then we write [MATH: A \neq B.] For example,
[MATH: \{ 1,2,3 \} \neq \{ 4 \}.]
